contracts.docstring: Identify one packaged SQL step or the specialized atomic rebuild it requires.
Apply this trusted catalog step through its original transactional implementation.
Validate the requested supported forward boundary before opening or creating storage.
Refuse future schemas, incomplete modern prefixes and implicit reversal without changing data.
Build the real pre-wiki-migration schema without copying a production database.
Default fixtures to current schema; historical tests explicitly select a forward prefix.
Seed real scoped coordination storage at the explicitly selected supported schema version.
Retain a schema-only run and original attempt using columns present since version34.
Seed a version49 execution with two task references and retained original JSON bytes.
Seed closed version41 author/reviewer references for inverse preservation tests only.
A version27 receipt stays historical after upgrades without inventing admission evidence.
A failed schema54 install leaves schema53 and old work intact; retry adds guards without minting native proof.
Normal startup installs the typed publication schema, keeps accepted provenance and prevents retargeting its immutable original request.
Upgrade a coherent version26 without inventing ownership for old command history.
The kind expansion keeps primary identities and foreign keys instead of renaming the runs table.
Development/review identity is actual stored data; this is schema evidence, not a writable runtime proof.
Two different author kinds cannot race for the same task, nor can two review kinds.
Version42 removal preserves closed review bytes and rejects retained owner history without deleting it.
Start from the actual version42 prefix and remove only unused later structures before testing inverses.
Downgrade keeps original identities and schema objects and can be reapplied without loss.
Even a closed or interrupted preparation is retained evidence, not disposable empty schema.
Removing empty workspace storage does not authorize reinterpretation of an execution or an unclosed scope.
Build the complete version35 prefix through the production migration catalog.
Upgrade actual historical rows and child references without inventing preparation evidence.
An invalid new SQL tail cannot publish a partial index, column, table or migration marker.
A failed schema52 install rolls back its table/guards; a repeatable successful upgrade preserves actual schema51 historical records.
Compare schema and retained business rows independently of WAL pages and file layout.
Reach every supported post-legacy version, then repeat startup without losing IDs or relations.
Abruptly kill only a new migration child before its history insert, then recover that same DB.
Unknown targets and booleans cannot create a partial installation as a side effect.
A forward migration cannot hide a future version, fill a fabricated gap or act as downgrade.
A failed migration cannot leave rebuilt half-tables; upgrading an actual schema49 preserves original identities and exact handoff bytes.
A failed schema51 install cannot change existing manifests or replace the old invalidation view; successful retry retains exact original intent and foreign keys.
Build a version23 fixture without newer rebuilds changing the migration under test.
A downgrade cannot erase a delivery or remove a capability while its authority remains live.
Retain unknown input on a version29 dispatch across repeatable upgrades.
A failed schema53 install leaves schema52 data/guards intact; a repeatable retry preserves historical scientific completion without inventing acceptance.
Preserve version28 rows and record only future edits after upgrading.

Run pending schema migrations for existing databases.

Checks the ``schema_migrations`` table and applies any missing
migrations. Safe to call multiple times. Serving requires an already
initialized file; explicit installation/legacy callers may create one.
Explicit forward targets support staged upgrades; serving always defaults
to the latest schema. A target never authorizes an implicit downgrade.
